content.user_title: Plan Feature Work with Clear Implementation Tasks
content.value_statement: Feature ideas often fail because requirements and task boundaries stay unclear. This skill turns discovery answers into a structured implementation plan.
actual_capabilities: Guides Socratic discovery with goal, success, constraint, and alternative questions.
Turns requirements into a discovery summary with decisions and open questions.
Creates implementation plan sections for goals, stack, dependencies, and files.
Breaks work into small test-first tasks with commit message guidance.
Defines a simple workflow from discovery to plan to execution.
limitations: It provides planning guidance only; it does not implement code directly.
It depends on the user to supply product goals and constraints.
It does not verify repository paths unless the agent reads the codebase.
It does not replace project management or architecture review for complex programs.

use_cases.title: Plan a new product feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature idea into goals, constraints, decisions, files, tests, and task steps.

use_cases.title: Clarify vague stakeholder requests
use_cases.description: Use focused questions to identify success measures, limits, alternatives, and unresolved decisions.

use_cases.title: Prepare work for another engineer
use_cases.description: Create a plan that explains context, file changes, test work, and commit boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Start discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a vague feature idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the planning skill for this feature: [feature idea]. Ask discovery questions first. Wait for my answers before writing a plan.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert answers into a clear discovery summary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my notes to write a discovery summary. Include core requirements, technical decisions, constraints, alternatives, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Write implementation plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a plan for an engineer with little context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for [feature]. Assume the engineer lacks context. Include goal, stack, affected files, tests, tasks, and commits.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an advanced plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing plan before execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this implementation plan for gaps. Make tasks smaller, add missing tests, identify risky assumptions, and preserve clear commit boundaries.

output_examples.input: Plan password reset for an existing web application.
output: Discovery questions cover identity proof, token expiry, email delivery, abuse limits, and success metrics.
The plan lists affected account, email, form, and test areas.
Tasks separate token generation, request flow, reset flow, validation, and user messaging.

output_examples.input: Prepare a migration from one payment provider to another.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a discovery summary, compares migration approaches, lists open risks, and breaks implementation into test-first tasks.

output_examples.input: Turn a short feature request into work for a new contractor.
output_examples.output: The result explains the goal, expected files, required tests, task order, and commit messages in plain language.

best_practices: Answer discovery questions before asking for the final implementation plan.
Provide repository context when file paths, frameworks, or dependencies matter.
Review open questions before execution so hidden assumptions do not enter the task list.
anti_patterns: Do not skip discovery when the feature goal or success measure is unclear.
Do not treat example file paths as verified repository paths.
Do not use the plan as a substitute for security, compliance, or architecture review.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates implementation plans and task breakdowns for later coding work.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before feature development, especially when requirements are vague or several approaches are possible.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need repository access?
faq.answer: Repository access helps when the plan needs exact files, dependencies, or tests.

faq.question: Can it handle non-technical requests?
faq.answer: It can clarify goals and constraints, but its plan format is aimed at software implementation.

faq.question: How detailed are the tasks?
faq.answer: The source skill recommends small tasks, usually sized for two to five minutes of focused work.
